product_family: SkedPal is a single-product AI calendar / auto-scheduling tool that turns to-do lists into time-blocked schedules; no separate enterprise, API, or self-hosted tier was found, just individual and team (via calendar/Asana integration) usage of the same web/desktop/mobile app.

certifications.name: SOC 2 (Type 1/2)
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence. No trust center, security page, or SOC 2 mention found on skedpal.com home page, privacy policy, or terms of use; www.skedpal.com/security returns 404.

certifications.name: ISO 27001
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence. Not referenced anywhere on the vendor's own pages.

certifications.name: GDPR
certifications.proof_quote: Policy references cross-border transfer language ('Personal information may be transferred to and processed in the United Arab Emirates, where data protection laws may differ from your jurisdiction') but makes no explicit GDPR-compliance commitment, no mention of a DPA, EU representative, or data-subject-rights process. Graded as an unconfirmed/weak GDPR posture rather than a held certification.

certifications.name: HIPAA
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence. Not referenced anywhere on the vendor's own pages; product is a personal/team scheduling tool, not positioned for regulated health data.

certifications.name: PCI DSS
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence. Terms of use note that billing/credit-card data may be 'shared with third parties for transaction processing' (i.e. handed off to a payment processor) but do not state SkedPal itself holds PCI DSS certification.

certifications.name: ISO/IEC 42001 (AI governance)
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence. No AI-specific governance, model-training, or AI-security disclosure found on any vendor page despite the product being marketed as 'The AI Calendar'.

certifications.name: FedRAMP
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence; not a plausible fit for a consumer/SMB scheduling tool.

privacy.ai_training_note: SkedPal markets itself as an 'AI Calendar' but neither the home page nor the privacy policy discloses how AI/auto-scheduling processes user task and calendar data, whether any model is trained on customer data, or whether an opt-out exists. Could not confirm either way; treated as unknown rather than assumed no.
privacy.data_region: United Arab Emirates (privacy policy: 'Personal information may be transferred to and processed in the United Arab Emirates, where data protection laws may differ from your jurisdiction')

security.name: Encryption in transit/at rest
security.value: Not specified. Privacy policy only states 'no method of transmission over the Internet, or method of electronic storage is 100% secure' and that the company uses 'commercially acceptable means' to protect data - no concrete encryption standard (e.g. TLS 1.2+, AES-256) is documented.

security.name: Formal security certifications
security.value: None published. No trust center, no SOC 2/ISO badges, /security path 404s.

security.name: Third-party data sharing
security.value: Privacy policy states data is not shared except as described, with named use of Google Analytics as a data processor; payment data is shared with third-party processors per the terms of use.

security.name: Breach notification
security.value: Terms of use place the burden on the user to notify SkedPal of any security breach or unauthorized account use immediately; no vendor-side breach-notification commitment to customers is documented.

products.name: SkedPal (web/desktop/mobile app)
products.category: AI calendar / auto-scheduling and task time-blocking tool
products.data_scope: User task lists, calendar data (via two-way sync with Google/Outlook-type calendars and Asana), account/profile info, device and usage data, payment/billing details for subscriptions
products.notes: Single product tier structure (individual free trial -> paid subscription); 'team' usage is only via collaborative integration with Asana, not a distinct enterprise product with its own security posture. No API product or self-hosted option found.

compare.pricing_model: Subscription (14-day free trial, then paid plans; no public enterprise/custom pricing tier found)
compare.data_residency: United Arab Emirates (per privacy policy transfer clause); no region-choice or EU-hosting option disclosed

flags: No trust center or dedicated security page (skedpal.com/security returns 404); all security posture had to be inferred from a boilerplate privacy policy and terms of use.

Product is marketed as an 'AI Calendar' but discloses nothing about how AI/scheduling algorithms process user data or whether it is used for model training - flagged as an AI-training transparency gap.

Data is processed in the United Arab Emirates per the vendor's own privacy policy; this is a data-residency point AIFOXX should surface to EU/US enterprise buyers, since no DPA or SCC mechanism is mentioned.

Minor legal-entity naming inconsistency: privacy policy names 'Tempus Computer Systems Design, LLC' while the terms of use refers to the same company as 'Tempus Systems' - treated as the same entity but noted for the record.
